comment: Good professor for an intro econ class, good amount of work and tests were perfectly challenging. Overall, would recommend.
Very fair professor. It's not difficult to succeed as long as you pay attention in class and do the homework.

I enjoyed her class. She was always accessible outside of class and willing to help you understand anything you were confused about. The homework was very manageable, and the tests are easy if you pay attention in class. The class is mostly lectures, which can be confusing at times, but there are also group activities, and she encourages questions.

Professor Gupta is one of the worst professors I've encountered in college. She is unhelpful and inaccessible. Midterms are confusing and long. Grading feels extremely subjective. Behavioral Economics is interesting, but the lectures are boring. I ended up hating the class.

professor gupta's lectures are incomprehensible and she confuses herself more than her already puzzled studente. her tests are graded based on vibes (all open ended with no clear critera) and her homeworks are long and graded with 2 attempts per question. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

Worst teacher ever. Genuinely don't know how she got hired as a professor since she doesn't even know what she's talking about. Her lectures make no sense and don't relate to what's on the exam. Might as well learn by yourself since going to her class will confuse you more.

I thoroughly enjoyed the class, although it is very lecture heavy. The homework is not bad at all and doesn't take too long. For the tests, it is all open ended questions, which actually isn't that bad because she gives lots of partial credit, and the review packets we do in class are pretty similar.

Took her for ECON101--if you want to just skip lecture and teach yourself you can because she doesn't take attendance and posts videos, but if you want to actually go and learn you are better off with another professor because she overcomplicates the hell out of everything. Two midterms, I did significantly better on the one where I taught myself.

Lectures make no sense. When I go to office hours to ask a question or go over something she either talks to me like I'm stupid or refuses to answer the question. She dosent answer emails either. Dont take her

I took this professor for Behavioral Econ, she was great. She was available outside of class and responded quickly to questions. I found the topic very interesting and I didn't think I would at the beginning of the semester. There is a couple papers but they are really easy and are normally just bullet points answering questions. Highly recommended

Dr. Gupta is a wonderful conversationalist and genuinely cares about her students. The work is tough but she is ready and willing to work with each student to help them understand. Her office hours are accessible and she is happy to talk for as long as you need. I'm not an econ whiz but she made me love the class. Amazing professor, I recommend!

Professor Gupta cares about her students' feedback and gives a lot of extra credit during the semester. All the tests are written, and cumulative and she does partial grading, so if you know the material well you will be fine.

Dr. Gupta is great, she's very caring and actually makes sure everyone understands the information. She does in-class games that help us actually understand the topics. If you keep up in class the homework is not bad at all and neither are the tests. I feel like I learned a good bit of economics from this class.

Professor can make topics much more confusing than they are and I often would leave class much more confused than when I entered. If you're already familiar with the topic and prefer to teach yourself majority of the material then you will do fine in the class. Professor can be very intimidating at times and she gives assigned seats.
Dr. G is very nice. She is smart but sometimes has a hard time getting you to understand concepts the way she does, and gets frustrated when nobody gets it.

Dr. G is a compassionate professor who cares about her students learning. She truly cares if her students understand the material intuitively rather than by memorization. Tests are reasonable and straightforward, but you must study quite a bit. Homework can take a lot of time, but it's assigned a week in advance.

Read the textbook and study a lot for tests and you will do well. She often makes mistakes or gets confused during lectures which ends up confusing you more but if you put in the time for exams you will do well. Weekly homework is online and kinda difficult but she gave extra credit at the end of the semester.
Confusing teaching
Sometimes the lessons were confusing, but you could tell she really cares about her students and their ability to succeed.

Dr. G is a great professor and a very kind person. Some of her lectures were confusing because she overcomplicated the concept she was teaching, but everything was generally easy to follow. There are a few homework assignments every week, but they aren't overwhelming. Tests are a big part of your grade. Overall, this was a good class.

Dr. G was great since I'd never taken micro-econ before. Others who had taken some econ in high school said she over-explained things which often led to confusion. Homework didn't always line up perfectly with lecture. Grading structure was a little weird, your grade is determined by how many points you get off the whole semester.
